title: desktop liberator hardcodes its gsettings keys and values and swallows every failure
body:
`liberators/desktop.sh` lines 139 to 150 set a dozen GNOME keys with literal values written into the liberator: `org.gnome.mutter overlay-key` to empty, the `org.gnome.desktop.wm.keybindings` switchers to Alt-Tab and Shift-Alt-Tab, `panel-main-menu` to none, and the `media-keys` screenreader and magnifier bindings to none. Two things are wrong with that block.

- The keys and values are Molt's, not the user's. Every other preference a sleeve carries comes from Molt-matts and renders per host; these cannot be changed, added to or dropped without editing the framework, and a second user of Molt gets Matt's GNOME bindings.
- Every `gsettings set` ends `2>/dev/null || true`, so a key that no longer exists, a schema that is not installed, or a value GNOME refuses is silent, and `molt upgrade` says the sleeve is ready over a binding that did not take (the No Silent Errors shape; `check` cannot see the gap either, since it reads back only `overlay-key` and the favourites).

Fix, when it is picked up: the key/value pairs move into the user stack, as a `[desktop]` table or a `config/desktop/gsettings.toml` beside the favourites file, read with `molt_liberator_field` or the same TOML reader; the liberator applies what the stack declares, reads each value back and names any that did not take, and `check` compares all of them, not one. Carried from the vc board's small items on 22 Oct 2026; low, since kovacs is the only GNOME sleeve and its bindings are right.


## As built (22 Oct 2026)

Merged to main as 38d7717 from issue-0035 8927469 (cc); Molt-matts e1d09a1 from 0747b42 adds `instances/kovacs/desktop/gsettings` with the ten pairs the block had set, in gsettings' print form. The hardcoded block is gone from `liberators/desktop.sh`. The keys come from `instances/<host>/desktop/gsettings`, found like the favourites file through the shared `_desktop_instance_file`: one `<schema> <key> <value>` per line, the value to the end of the line as `gsettings get` prints it, blank lines and lines starting with `#` ignored (a `#` later in a line is part of the value); a line with fewer than three fields is a fault naming the file and line, and install stops before setting anything. Install tries every pair, letting gsettings' words through: a refused set is an error naming schema and key; a key that cannot be read back is its own error; a read-back that differs is "did not take: wanted X, got Y"; GTK and favourites still run, then install fails. `check` and `verify` compare every declared pair against `gsettings get`'s stdout (a GLib warning beside a value is not drift), naming each that differs with wanted and got. Tests in `test/liberators/desktop.bats` with a fake gsettings. The guide's templates table has the file's row (ac, 1513fb7). The merged tree passed under brew bash and /bin/bash 3.2, shellcheck clean, and the branch's tests were red on main's code. Not verified on GNOME by anyone yet: the kovacs values' print forms; kovacs-sysadm's upgrade to v0.2.0 proves them, and a mismatch shows as "did not take". Left for later, below the gate: check and verify pass silently when a file is declared but gsettings is absent, as the favourites do; the instance-path build repeated across lib/molt.sh, lib/agent.sh, ssh.sh and keys.sh. CI run 39810039184 green.
